ESTABLISHING A RIGHT TO FARM AND RANCH POLICY  
\YHEREAS. the Board of County Commissioners of Fremont County (Board) recognizes 
the importance of ranching, farming, and other agricultural activities and operations on Fremont 
County, including the protection of the visibility of such activities; and 
'WHEREAS, the changing nature of land use ~n'd 'demography in particular parts of and 
throughout Fremont County has increased the potential of conflicts between agricultural 
operators, county visitors and residents of nlral Fremont County. which may threaten the 
continued economic viability of agricultural operations in the county; and 
'WHEREAS, examples of such conflicts include but are not limited to: harassment of 
livestock and livestock losses due to free roaming dogs; trespass by livestock; livestock on 
highways ancl county roads; gates left open; fence construction and maintenance; chemical 
application; maintenance of ditches across private property and burning ditches; complaints 
about noise, dust and odor; disposal of dead animals; weecls and pest control; trespass; and 
movement of machinery on highways and county roads; ancl 
\VI-IEREAS, it is desirable to protect agricultural operators" from complaints about legal  
and non-negligent agricultural operations and activities; and  
'WHEREAS. it is desirable to educate the public and non-agticultural. residents and 
visitors to Fremont County about the existence, value and importance of the county's agricultural 
operations ancl activities; and 
.
